title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples Recognition (Sunset Extension) Bill 2015
short_title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples Recognition (Sunset Extension) Bill 2015

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Argued in support of extending the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples Recognition Act by three years to maintain momentum toward a constitutional recognition referendum, recalled the 1967 referendum and the recent death of campaigner Faith Bandler, and called for removal of section 25 of the Constitution.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: Supported extending the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples Recognition Act's sunset date by three years to 28 March 2018, traced the decades-long campaign for constitutional recognition including the 1967 referendum in which over 90 per cent of Australians voted yes, and paid tribute to campaigner Faith Bandler, recently farewelled at a funeral service.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Supported extending the recognition act's sunset date, noted only eight of 44 referenda since 1906 have passed, the last on 21 May 1977, and said 4.7 per cent of people in his electorate of Riverina identified as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander at the 2011 census.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: Supported extending the recognition act, recalled how the landmark Mabo decision on 3 June 1992 overturned the doctrine of terra nullius, and said Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have an enduring connection to country going back at least 40,000 years.

speeches.speaker: Ken Wyatt
speeches.brief: Supported extending the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples Recognition Act to 28 March 2018, noted the bill was first introduced by then minister Jenny Macklin in 2012, and said the joint select committee has recommended removing sections 25 and 51(xxvi) of the Constitution, which reference race.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: Supported extending the recognition act, noted only eight of 44 Australian referendums have succeeded, contrasted the 1967 referendum's more than 90 per cent yes vote with the failed 1999 republic referendum where about 54 per cent voted no, and called for better funded community education ahead of a future vote.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Supported extending the recognition act, recounted the 1939 Cummeragunja walk-off in which about 200 Indigenous people left a New South Wales mission, and honoured two South Australians, Gallipoli veteran Hubert Tripp and his cousin Marj Tripp, the first Aboriginal woman to join the Royal Australian Navy in 1963.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Supported extending the recognition act, recalled that 5,700,000 Australians, or 91 per cent, voted yes in the 1967 referendum, quoted Western Australia's 1944 Native Citizenship Rights Act which required Aboriginal people to renounce family ties beyond immediate kin to gain citizenship, and cited painter Albert Namatjira, whose citizenship was revoked after he shared alcohol with relatives.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: Summed up debate on the recognition act extension, noted only eight of 44 constitutional referenda have ever succeeded, said the government aims for support similar to the 1967 referendum's 90 per cent yes vote, and noted 2017 will mark that referendum's 50th anniversary.

acts.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples Recognition (Sunset Extension) Act 2015
